info.title: CueRCode API
info.description:
REST API for generating, customising, and downloading QR codes. The CueRCode web UI is built ON TOP OF this API, so the API is the contract and the UI is just one client: every feature available in the UI is available here.

The API supports 26 QR code types and multiple output formats (PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF), custom colours and gradients, module and finder-pattern (marker) shapes, logo overlays, decorative frames with labels, error-correction selection, sizing, and an optional quiet zone.

## Authentication

The API supports two authentication methods (either satisfies a protected endpoint):

1. **API Key** - Include your API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Format: `cuercode_` followed by 40 hexadecimal characters. Obtain one from the admin panel.
2. **CSRF Token** - For web UI AJAX requests, include the session CSRF token in the `X-CSRF-Token` header.

Protected endpoints (`/generate`, `/preview`, `/download/{uuid}`, `/save`, `/qrcodes`, `/qrcodes/{uuid}`) require ONE of the above. Anonymous endpoints (`/bulk-generate`, `/types`, `/formats`, `/health`) require no authentication but are still rate limited.

## Saved-Codes Library (Epic E3 stage 2a)

`POST /save` claims a previously-generated QR code (by its `uuid`) into the authenticated caller's account, subject to the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`402 SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED` at/over the cap). `GET /qrcodes` lists ONLY the caller's own saved codes (paginated, optionally filtered by `type`). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /qrcodes/{uuid}` operate on a single saved code: ownership is re-checked on every request from the caller's authenticated identity, never from a client-supplied field. A code that is neither owned by the caller nor marked `is_public` is reported as `404` (never `403`) to avoid disclosing that a private UUID belonging to someone else exists. `DELETE` soft-deletes (frees a `saved_codes` slot; the row is retained for audit purposes). `is_public: true` (opt-in; default `false`) grants read/download access to any authenticated caller but never write access - only the owner may `PATCH`/`DELETE`.

## Rate Limiting

All endpoints are rate limited (the `/health` endpoint is exempt in practice). Rate limit headers are included on every rate-limited response:
- `X-RateLimit-Limit` - Maximum requests per minute
- `X-RateLimit-Remaining` - Remaining requests in the current window
- `X-RateLimit-Reset` - Unix epoch time (seconds) at which the window resets
- `Retry-After` - Seconds to wait before retrying (only on `429`)

## Request Body

POST request bodies must be sent with `Content-Type: application/json` (an optional charset parameter such as `; charset=utf-8` is permitted); otherwise the API responds with `415 Unsupported Media Type`. Request bodies larger than the configured maximum (256 KiB by default) are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large`. Per-field length caps also apply (type ≤ 64 chars, each input scalar ≤ 4096 chars, frame_label ≤ 120 chars) and over-long fields are rejected with `400 FIELD_TOO_LONG`.

## Response Format

By default, responses are in JSON. To receive XML instead, either:
- Set the `Accept` header to `application/xml`, or
- Add `?format=xml` to the query string.

XML responses share the same logical structure as JSON: a root `<response>` element wrapping `success`, `message`, `data`, optional `error_code`, and `timestamp`. Arrays serialise as repeated `<item>` elements.

## Output Formats

Supported formats: **PNG**, **JPG/JPEG**, **GIF**, **WebP**, **SVG**, and **PDF**. SVG additionally supports gradients and the extended (SVG-only) module/marker shapes; PDF is vector-only and does not support transparency, logo overlay, or frames.

**JPEG-XL (`jxl`) host limitation:** although the underlying schema reserves a `jxl` format value and the web server advertises the `image/jxl` MIME type, JPEG-XL is NOT an accepted `format` value on this deployment. The QR generation library / GD build on the Dreamhost host does not encode JPEG-XL, so requests asking for `jxl` are coerced to `png`. Use one of the six supported formats above.

post.description:
Generate a full QR code with customisations. The generated code is saved to the database and filesystem, and the response includes a base64 data URI image, UUID identifier, and download URL.

Requires authentication (API key OR CSRF token).

post.description:
Generate a smaller (300px) PNG preview of a QR code. The preview is not saved to the database or filesystem. Use this for real-time previews in the UI before generating the final QR code. The `format` and `size` of any supplied customisation are overridden (always PNG, 300px); all other customisation is honoured.

Requires authentication (API key OR CSRF token).

post.summary: Bulk generate QR codes (ZIP, or an Avery label-sheet PDF)
post.description:
Generate many QR codes in a single synchronous request and receive them as a ZIP archive (`application/zip`). This endpoint is anonymous-capable (no authentication required) but is rate limited and subject to the same request-body-size cap as the other POST endpoints.

Provide EITHER an `items` array OR a `csv` string. An optional request-level `customization` object supplies shared defaults that each item's own customization overrides key-by-key.

The maximum number of items per request depends on the caller's subscription plan (`bulk_batch_size` limit, Epic E4) — anonymous callers get the `anonymous` plan's allowance (25 by default), while an authenticated user or API key resolves their own plan's allowance instead; exceeding it returns `413` with an `upgrade_url` hint. Per-item failures do NOT abort the batch — each item's outcome is recorded in a `manifest.txt` file inside the ZIP, and successfully generated images are named `NNN-<type>.<ext>`.

If the server's PHP `zip` extension is not installed, the endpoint returns `501 Not Implemented`.

**Avery label-sheet PDF (E5 / #49):** when the REQUEST-LEVEL (shared) `customization` sets `format: pdf` and `pdf_layout` to `avery_5160` or `avery_l7160`, the response is a DIFFERENT shape entirely — a single combined `application/pdf` Avery label-sheet document (not a ZIP) with each item tiled into successive label slots, spanning extra sheet pages as needed. Per-item `pdf_layout`/`format` overrides are ignored in this mode (every item is forced onto the same sheet layout — a mixed-layout sheet is not a coherent single PDF); per-item failures leave that label slot blank rather than aborting the sheet. See the Customization `pdf_layout` field for the full enum.

items_array.summary: Explicit item list with shared defaults

200.description: ZIP archive of generated QR codes (plus manifest.txt) — OR, when the shared customization requests `format: pdf` with `pdf_layout: avery_5160`/`avery_l7160` (E5 / #49), a single combined Avery label-sheet `application/pdf` document instead. See the operation description.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for download (`cuercode-bulk.zip`, or `cuercode-bulk-avery_5160.pdf`/`cuercode-bulk-avery_l7160.pdf` for the Avery-sheet response)

X-Bulk-Failed.description: Number of items that failed (see manifest.txt, or left blank on the Avery sheet)

application/pdf.description: Returned instead of application/zip when pdf_layout is avery_5160/avery_l7160 (E5 / #49).

400.description: Invalid request (no items/csv, malformed item, bad CSV header)

value.message: Bulk request must include either an "items" array or a "csv" string.

413.description: Too many items (exceeds the caller's plan bulk_batch_size limit) or request body too large

422.description: Avery label-sheet mode only (E5 / #49): every item failed generation, so there is nothing to place on the sheet (error_code BULK_AVERY_ALL_FAILED)

501.description: Bulk ZIP generation unavailable (server missing the PHP zip extension)

value.message: Bulk ZIP generation is unavailable: the server is missing the PHP "zip" extension.

post.description: Create a new (pending) user account and queue an email-verification message. ANTI-ENUMERATION: this endpoint ALWAYS returns the same 201 response, whether the email address was brand new or already registered - the caller cannot distinguish the two outcomes. No new verification email is sent for an already-registered address. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

201.description: Registration request accepted (identical response regardless of whether the email was new or already registered)

value.message: If this email address is available for registration, a verification link has been sent to it.

post.summary: Log in and establish a session
post.description: Authenticate by email + password and, on success, issue a database-backed session (tblUserSessions) and regenerate the PHP session id. ANTI-ENUMERATION: every failure path (wrong password, no such account, locked account, unverified/pending account, suspended account) returns the IDENTICAL 401 response - none of these states are distinguishable from the outside. Failed attempts count towards an account lockout (security.max_login_attempts / security.lockout_duration). Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Login successful - a session has been established

value.message: Logged in successfully.

401.description: Invalid email or password, or the account is not yet verified (a single generic message covers every failure mode - see description above)

value.message: Invalid email or password, or the account is not yet verified.

post.description: Revoke the current database-backed session (if any) and rotate the PHP session id. Idempotent - calling this with no active session is a harmless no-op that still returns 200, so a status-code difference can never be used to probe session state. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Logged out (idempotent - returned even if there was no active session)

value.message: Logged out successfully.

post.description: Consume a single-use, expiring email-verification token (from the link emailed by POST /auth/register) and activate the owning account. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Email address verified; the account is now active

value.message: Your email address has been verified. You can now log in.

400.description: The token is invalid, not found, or has expired

value.message: This verification link is invalid or has expired.

post.description: Queue a password-reset email if (and only if) the address belongs to an active account. ANTI-ENUMERATION: ALWAYS returns the IDENTICAL 200 response regardless of whether the email is registered - this is a hard requirement (SECURITY.md), not an implementation detail. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Request accepted (identical response regardless of whether the email is registered)

value.message: If this email address is registered, a password reset link has been sent to it.

post.summary: Reset a password using an emailed token
post.description: Consume a single-use, expiring password-reset token (from the link emailed by POST /auth/request-password-reset) and set a new password. All existing sessions for the account are revoked on success. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key.

200.description: Password reset - all existing sessions for the account have been revoked

value.message: Your password has been reset. You can now log in with your new password.

400.description: Missing fields, or the token is invalid/not found/expired

value.message: This password reset link is invalid or has expired.

post.summary: Save a generated QR code to your account
post.description: Claim a previously-generated QR code (by the `uuid` returned from POST /generate) into the authenticated caller's account, or - if the caller already owns it - update its label/visibility. Enforces the caller's plan `saved_codes` limit (`-1` = unlimited) ONLY for a genuinely NEW claim; re-saving an already-owned code never consumes a fresh slot. A code already claimed by a DIFFERENT user is reported as `404` (never `403`/`409` at this stage) to avoid disclosing that the UUID belongs to somebody else. Requires a valid CSRF token (web UI) or API key belonging to an authenticated account.

200.description: An already-owned code's label/visibility was updated

201.description: The code was newly claimed into the caller's account

value.message: QR code saved to your account.

404.description: The UUID does not exist, has been deleted, or is already saved to a DIFFERENT account (indistinguishable from not-found - see description above)

value.message: QR code not found.

409.description: Lost a race to a concurrent claim of the same code

429.description: Too many requests. Two distinct causes share this status code on `/save` specifically: (1) the router's generic per-key/per-IP rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), or (2) `SAVE_LOCK_BUSY` - the per-user `saved_codes` advisory lock (SECURITY.md F-023, closing a plan-limit TOCTOU race) timed out because another `/save` request for this SAME account is already mid-flight. Both include a `Retry-After` header; back off and retry.

value.message: Rate limit exceeded. Please wait before making another request.
The saved-codes service is busy processing another request for your account. Please try again shortly.

get.description: Lists ONLY the authenticated caller's own saved QR codes - never another user's rows, public or otherwise. Supports pagination (`page`, `per_page`, capped at 100) and an optional `type` filter matching the QR code type name.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page number (default 1; clamped up to 1 if lower)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter to a single QR code type name (e.g. "url", "wifi")

200.description: The caller's saved QR codes, paginated

get.description: Allowed only if the caller owns the code OR it is marked `is_public: true` - otherwise `404` (never `403`, to avoid disclosing that a private UUID belonging to someone else exists).

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The QR code (caller owns it, or it is public)

404.description: Not found, deleted, or not owned-and-not-public (identical response for all three - see description above)

value.message: QR code not found.

patch.summary: Update a saved QR code you own
patch.description: Update the `label`, `is_public` visibility, and/or visual `customization` of a saved code the caller OWNS. Ownership is checked BEFORE any other field is read - a non-owned code (including a PUBLIC one; `is_public` never grants write access) is reported as `404`. When `customization` is supplied, the QR image is regenerated in place from the code's existing payload (its `download_url`/`uuid` do not change) and `qrFilePath`/`qrOptions`/`qrOutputFormat` are updated. Content/destination changes are out of scope for this stage.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The saved QR code was updated

404.description: Not owned by the caller (or does not exist / was deleted) - identical response either way

delete.summary: Delete a saved QR code you own
delete.description: Soft-deletes (sets `deletedAt`; the row is retained for audit purposes) a saved code the caller OWNS, freeing one `saved_codes` plan slot. Ownership is checked before any mutation; a non-owned code is reported as `404`.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: The UUID v4 identifier of the saved QR code

200.description: The saved QR code was deleted

value.message: QR code deleted successfully.

404.description: Not owned by the caller (or does not exist / already deleted) - identical response either way

plan_limit.description: The caller's current plan limit for this action (-1 = unlimited, so this response is unreachable at -1)

value.message: You have reached your plan's saved-codes limit (25). Upgrade your plan to save more codes.

type.description: The QR code type identifier (one of 26 supported types). Use the /types endpoint to retrieve the definitive active list and each type's form field schema. Maximum 64 characters.

input.description: Type-specific input data. The required fields depend on the QR code type; use /types to obtain the form schema for each type. Each scalar field is limited to 4096 characters. Examples: url -> {"url":"https://example.com"}; wifi -> {"ssid":"...","password":"...","encryption":"WPA","hidden":false}; vcard -> {"first_name":"John","last_name":"Doe",...}; geo -> {"latitude":51.5074,"longitude":-0.1278,"label":"London"}; gs1_product -> {"gtin":"09521234543213","batch":"LOT42"}.

Customization.description: Visual customisation options for the QR code. All fields are optional; defaults are applied for missing values. The same object is accepted at the request level for bulk generation (as shared defaults) and per item/row (overriding the shared defaults key-by-key). Unknown keys are ignored.

format.description: Output image format. `jpeg` is an accepted alias of `jpg`. Note: JPEG-XL (`jxl`) is NOT accepted on this host (see the API description); an unrecognised value falls back to `png`.

size.description: Target image size in pixels (width/height). Clamped to the 100-4000 range server-side. Ignored by /preview (always 300px).

ecc.description: Error correction level. L=7%, M=15%, Q=25%, H=30% recovery. Higher levels tolerate more damage/obstruction. The API default is M (the web UI defaults to H). Use H when adding a logo.

fg_color.description: Foreground (dark module) colour as a hex code (#RGB, #RRGGBB, or #RRGGBBAA).

bg_color.description: Background (light module) colour as a hex code.

marker_color.description: Finder pattern (corner squares) colour as a hex code. Optional; defaults to the foreground colour when omitted or empty.

pattern.description: Module (pixel) shape style. The square/round/dot set applies to all raster and SVG output; additional decorative shapes (diamond/star/heart) are SVG-only.

oneOf.description: Predefined logo ID from the logo library (tblPredefinedLogos).
`upload` to use a custom logo supplied via logo_data, or a logo identifier/path.

logo.description: Logo to overlay on the QR code centre. Using a logo automatically upgrades ECC to H. Set to `upload` and provide logo_data + logo_mime for a custom image.

logo_data.description: Base64-encoded custom logo as a data URI (e.g. `data:image/png;base64,...`). Used only when `logo` is `upload`.

logo_mime.description: MIME type of the uploaded custom logo. Used only when `logo` is `upload`.

logo_size_pct.description: Logo size as a percentage of the QR code dimensions. Clamped server-side (the API clamps to 10-40; the UI slider exposes 5-40).

frame_style.description: Decorative frame style drawn around the QR code. Label/banner/pill styles render the frame_label text. Not applied to PDF output.

frame_label.description: Text label for label/banner/pill frame styles (e.g. 'SCAN ME'). Maximum 120 characters (the UI limits this to 30).

frame_color.description: Frame border/background colour as a hex code.

transparent.description: Whether the background should be transparent. Honoured for PNG, GIF, WebP, and SVG; ignored for JPEG and PDF.

quiet_zone.description: Whether to include the quiet zone (the white margin around the QR code) that improves scanning reliability.

version.description: Optional fixed QR code version (1-40) controlling the module grid size (modules = 4 * version + 17). When omitted, the smallest version that fits the payload at the chosen ECC level is selected automatically.

preset.description: Customisation preset. `none` (default) applies no additional rules. `accessible` enforces an accessibility-focused configuration per ISO/IEC 18004 + WCAG 2.1: forces `ecc` to `H`, forces `quiet_zone` to `true`, DROPS any pinned `version` so the smallest auto-fit version is used, and evaluates the WCAG contrast ratio of `fg_color`/`bg_color`. A contrast ratio below 3:1 causes the request to be REJECTED with HTTP 422 (error_code `ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW`); a ratio from 3:1 up to (but not including) 4.5:1 is allowed through but reported as a non-blocking warning in the response `data.metadata.contrast_warning` field. See the /generate 422 response for a worked example.

scan_distance_cm.description: Optional intended scanning distance in centimetres, used only to compute a recommended physical print size via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (recommended size ≈ scan distance / 10, with a 20mm practical floor). When supplied together with `preset: accessible`, the recommendation is returned in the response as `data.metadata.recommended_print_size_mm`. Has no effect on the generated image itself.

gradient.description: Gradient fill for the dark modules (SVG output only). Advanced feature; not exposed in the standard web UI. Ignored for non-SVG formats.

pdf_layout.description: Print layout for `format: pdf` (E5 / #49). Ignored for any other format. `standard` (default) is today's unchanged QR-only PDF, byte-for-byte. `accessible_caption` adds a large-print (>=18pt) human-readable caption plus a Grade-1 (uncontracted) Braille caption line, rendered as geometric dot patterns (not a Unicode Braille font - core PDF fonts have no Braille glyphs). `tactile` includes everything in `accessible_caption` PLUS a second, clearly-delineated page containing CueRCode's own tactile locator frame overlay guide (registration marks + orientation dot), meant to be reproduced via swell paper, a Braille embosser, or a UV-varnish/raised-ink pass aligned with page 1 - this is an original design, not a reproduction of any third-party patented locator. `avery_5160` (US Letter, 3x10) and `avery_l7160` (A4, 3x7) tile the code into an Avery address-label sheet; on `/generate` a single code fills exactly ONE label with the rest of the sheet left blank as a printable template, while `/bulk-generate` (see BulkGenerateRequest) tiles MULTIPLE items across successive labels/pages when the SAME `pdf_layout` is set at the request level. See `/accessibility` on the web UI for the print/embossing best-practice guide.

BulkItem.description: A single QR code request inside a bulk batch.

type.description: The QR code type identifier (e.g., 'url', 'text', 'wifi'). See GenerateRequest.type for the full enum.

input.description: Type-specific input data for this item.

customization.description: Per-item customization. Overrides the request-level shared customization key-by-key.

BulkGenerateRequest.description: A bulk generation request. Provide EITHER an 'items' array OR a 'csv' string. An optional request-level 'customization' object supplies shared defaults that each item's own customization overrides.

items.description: Explicit list of QR code requests. Mutually exclusive with 'csv'.

csv.description: CSV body whose first non-empty line is the header row. The header must contain a 'type' column and at least one input column. Columns named 'input.<field>' (or any non-reserved column) become input fields; reserved columns (format, size, ecc, fg_color, bg_color, marker_color, pattern, logo, logo_size_pct, frame_style, frame_label, frame_color, transparent) fold into that row's customization. Mutually exclusive with 'items'.

customization.description: Shared customization defaults applied to every item (overridden by per-item/per-row customization).

uuid.description: Unique identifier for the generated QR code. Use this with the /download endpoint.

image.description: Base64 data URI of the generated QR code image

download_url.description: Relative URL for downloading the QR code file

mime_type.description: MIME type of the generated image

image.description: Base64 data URI of the preview image (always PNG, 300px)

AccessibleMetadata.description: Present in /generate and /preview responses ONLY when the request's customization.preset was 'accessible' (E5 / #48). Absent entirely for preset=none (the default).

accessible.description: Always true when this object is present.

contrast_ratio.description: The WCAG contrast ratio computed between fg_color and bg_color, rounded to 2 decimal places. Range 1.0-21.0.

contrast_warning.description: Present ONLY when 3:1 <= contrast_ratio < 4.5:1 - a non-blocking accessibility warning (requests below 3:1 are rejected with HTTP 422 instead; see the /generate 422 response).
contrast_warning.example: Contrast ratio 3.5:1 is below the recommended WCAG AA level of 4.5:1. Consider a higher-contrast colour pair for maximum readability.

recommended_print_size_mm.description: Recommended minimum print size (width = height) in millimetres, computed from the request's scan_distance_cm via the 10:1 scan-distance rule (20mm practical floor). Null when scan_distance_cm was not supplied.

count.description: Total number of active QR code types

name.description: Type identifier (use this in the 'type' field of generate/preview requests)

icon.description: FontAwesome icon class for UI rendering

description.description: Brief description of the QR code type
description.example: Open a website or web page

form_fields.description: Form field schema defining the input fields for this type (name, label, type, required, validation, etc.)

payload_template.description: Template showing the generated payload format, or null when the type is built by a dedicated payload builder.

description.example: PNG image (lossless compression, transparent background support)

supports_transparency.description: Whether the format supports transparent backgrounds

supports_logo.description: Whether the format supports logo overlay

supports_frame.description: Whether the format supports frame rendering

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code for programmatic handling. Known codes include: MISSING_FIELD, FIELD_TOO_LONG, INVALID_JSON, INVALID_CUSTOMIZATION, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, GENERATION_FAILED, AUTH_REQUIRED, INVALID_API_KEY, INVALID_CSRF_TOKEN, NOT_FOUND, ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND, METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, FETCH_ERROR, SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, ZIP_UNAVAILABLE, BULK_NO_INPUT, BULK_INVALID_ITEMS, BULK_EMPTY, BULK_INVALID_ITEM, BULK_INVALID_CSV, BULK_CSV_NO_HEADER, BULK_CSV_NO_TYPE, BULK_CSV_NO_INPUT, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_TYPE, BULK_ITEM_MISSING_INPUT, BULK_TOO_MANY_ITEMS, INVALID_EMAIL, WEAK_PASSWORD, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, VERIFICATION_TOKEN_INVALID, VERIFICATION_ALREADY_USED, RESET_TOKEN_INVALID, RESET_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED, CSRF_INVALID, HASH_FAILED, ACTIVATION_FAILED, RESET_FAILED, INVALID_UUID, INVALID_LABEL, NO_FIELDS, SAVED_CODES_LIMIT_REACHED, SAVE_CONFLICT, SAVE_FAILED, LIST_FAILED, UPDATE_FAILED, DELETE_FAILED, REGENERATION_FAILED, FILE_SAVE_FAILED, ACCESSIBLE_CONTRAST_TOO_LOW, SAVE_LOCK_BUSY.

token.description: The raw token from the emailed verification link
The raw token from the emailed reset link

new_password.example: a new correct horse battery staple

AuthGenericResponse.description: Generic success envelope used by every account/auth endpoint below. register/request-password-reset deliberately return an IDENTICAL shape regardless of whether the target account exists (anti user-enumeration, see SECURITY.md).

message.example: If this email address is available for registration, a verification link has been sent to it.

uuid.description: The UUID returned by a prior POST /generate call

label.description: Caller-supplied nickname for this saved code. Omit to leave unchanged; an explicit empty string or null clears it.

is_public.description: Opt-in: when true, this code becomes readable/downloadable by ANY authenticated caller, not just the owner. Defaults to false (private) for a NEW claim; omitted on an already-owned code leaves its current visibility unchanged.

message.example: QR code saved to your account.

QrCodeSummary.description: One saved QR code as returned by GET /qrcodes and GET /qrcodes/{uuid}. Never includes the owner's userID/email - a public code viewed by a non-owner must not disclose who owns it.

PatchQrCodeRequest.description: All fields optional, but at least one of label/is_public/customization must be present (else 400 NO_FIELDS). "customization" fields omitted from a partial update inherit the code's EXISTING stored value.
